topic: Why does changing a plain variable not update the screen?
hook_question: Why does your like button stay stuck at zero?

shots.speech: Ever wondered why your like button stays stuck at zero?
shots.visual: Phone mock with a social post; each tap on the like button fails and the count stays 0; status pill 'Still 0'.

shots.speech: React has one big idea that fixes this.
shots.visual: Title card: series label, 'useState', the promise line, three icon tiles.

shots.speech: Here's the code. Your likes sit in a plain variable, and each tap adds one.
shots.visual: Code window LikeButton.jsx, two lines highlighted in turn; status pill 'Plain variable'.

shots.speech: But on every re-render, React runs your component again from the top. The variable starts fresh, back to zero.
shots.visual: Entity card <LikeButton /> showing 1; a render sweep passes and the value drops back to 0.

shots.speech: Worse, changing a plain variable never tells React anything changed. So the screen never updates.
shots.visual: Entity card above a system panel 'React: Idle'; the connector between them is broken with an x.

shots.speech: use State fixes both. React keeps the value in its own memory and hands it back on every render.
shots.visual: System panel 'React' now holding a 'likes' slot; a pulse travels up the connector to the entity card.

shots.speech: And set Likes is the trigger. Call it, and React updates its memory, then re-renders using the new value.
shots.visual: Trigger chip setLikes(1) sends a pulse to the system panel; the slot goes 0 to 1; the entity card re-renders showing 1.

shots.speech: In code, use State of zero gives you two things: the value, and the setter that changes it.
shots.visual: Code map card: likes -> memory icon 'the current value'; setLikes -> bolt icon 'updates it and re-renders'.

shots.speech: Now every tap sticks. One, two, three likes!
shots.visual: The hook's phone mock again: each tap succeeds and the count climbs 1, 2, 3; status pill 'It works'.

shots.speech: Remember: re-renders reset plain variables. use State keeps the value. And the setter updates it and re-renders.
shots.visual: Takeaway list: three rows with the refresh, memory and bolt icons.

shots.speech: Follow for more, one idea at a time.
shots.visual: End card: Up next, Follow button, series chips.
